Routing opens without waiting for provider discovery and shows one role and choice at a time. Model names and patterns remain editable; private model and schema caches last 24 hours and retain the last successful results during refresh.

Select multiple catalog tools across filters and pages, choose package extras, and install them together. Catalogs show all results through 50 items, then use pages of 40. Each installation records its outcome, and retry handles only unfinished items.
Existing settings, advanced configuration and shared agent actions remain available. Queued installation selections survive interruption without automatically replaying work.

releases.title: Set up your chat before it starts
changes: New chat lives in the sidebar and opens a setup page. Choose the workspace, name, bundle and model before the first message; drafts and attachments survive reload without saving an empty chat.
Goals, modes and session controls are accessible beside the composer. The header holds chat details, the shared session ID and export controls.
The composer uses one Send/Stop button. It stops active work when the draft is empty and sends when text or attachments are present.
Canvas opens from an icon-only toolbar button. Unavailable older artifact sources no longer block the drawer, and their saved references remain intact for recovery.

releases.title: Work details from your event log
changes: Expanded work reads recorded tool inputs and results from native event logs, without another redaction pass, new payload copies or the old Tool completed placeholder.
Work sections appear between assistant replies in their actual order. Brief groups stay open, and actions no longer have nested disclosure controls or duplicate raw input/results.
Code blocks show all content through 15 lines, then preview the first 10. Copy keeps the complete content, and unavailable reads offer retry.
Choose time only, time with tokens and cost, or those details with tool/model call counts in Appearance. Group totals include earlier action pages and count cache writes once.
Live timing and usage survive delayed log writes and reloads. Existing native logs and historical saved content remain intact.

releases.title: Keep conversations ready after ecosystem updates
changes: Ecosystem updates and rollbacks now retire old workers while keeping the runtime available for your next message.
If a message cannot reach its worker, the conversation shows an error instead of staying marked as working. Delivery remains unconfirmed and no work is automatically replayed.

releases.title: Keep conversation names consistent across apps
changes: Web-created conversations now store their names where the Amplifier CLI reads them. Existing web names are adopted when a shared name is missing.
Renames from either interface remain visible when switching back. Background naming and later saves preserve your explicit choice, without changing saved messages or event history.
Unified and the updated CLI use Foundation for shared metadata and settings. Native session settings are included when the CLI resumes a conversation.

releases.title: Canvas within reach
changes: Open or close Canvas from a stable toggle at the far right of the top toolbar. Its active state follows the panel, and its icon follows the selected Canvas side.
Customize appearance, What the agent sees and Send feedback are grouped under More app options, with feedback attention indicators, keyboard navigation and focus return.
Narrow screens use accessible icon controls with touch targets. Saved artifacts, conversation drafts and unsaved Canvas edits retain the same shared user and agent protections.

releases.title: Keep Work and its ecosystem current
changes: Work and the bundled tools, context, live loop, skills and routing now follow their current branches instead of fixed commits.
Ecosystem checks include the conversation worker libraries. Updates prepare and validate a separate environment, then activate when work and calls are idle.
Rollback retains the installed dependency manifest and revisions, including after an app update or removal of a disposable runtime cache. New app dependency declarations appear as ecosystem updates.

releases.title: See the actual work behind each action
changes: Expand work to see commands and their output, exit codes, file contents and highlighted changes, task checklists, app actions, and delegated work.
Collapsed actions identify the command or file involved. Detailed timing, usage, call IDs, and original inputs and results remain available under Details, without repeated completion messages.

Streaming tool results are now retained correctly, including failures and empty output. Long saved content loads on expansion with retry and copy controls. Older steps whose content was never saved say so explicitly.

releases.title: Shared canvas awareness and reliable editing
changes: Agents receive small freshness notices for interactive surfaces when they next respond, including exact counts and pending edits. Ordinary drawing and control changes do not start model work.

Agents can selectively read current state, visible controls or drawing images. Images use the model's image format and remain separate from conversation text; unavailable or stale evidence is identified explicitly.

Generated surfaces can use a shared draft helper that saves completed edits before a question, retains failed saves and protects unfinished gestures. User and agent edits continue to share one tab and compatible state.

Drawing resize and tab changes preserve artwork. Older save acknowledgments cannot clear newer edits, and rendering errors remain visible until corrected. Chat drafts typed during first-conversation creation remain intact.
Saved conversation reconciliation avoids duplicated messages around steering, and context-limit failures preserve completed work with focused recovery guidance.

releases.title: A complete, easier-to-navigate settings experience
changes: Find every existing setting through a persistent sidebar, with separate Appearance, Voice, Notifications and Updates sections and focused pages for models, bundles, history and advanced controls.
Notifications retain server, private topic and access-token configuration. Smart Tools keeps catalog discovery, source installation, MCP connections, tool forms and interactive views.

Existing saved configuration, scoped defaults, generic bundle module editing and agent navigation remain compatible. Conversation diagnosis and safe recovery copies remain available from Current conversation. Unsaved private fields survive moving between settings sections while the dialog is open.
Notification refreshes and maintenance actions keep progress visible until completion. Mobile layouts, keyboard navigation, and shared or custom skins remain supported.

Sending clears the composer immediately and tracks pending delivery beside the message, with explicit retry or delivery checks. Message editing can continue in the current conversation or create a fork, preserving the original history.

releases.title: Use the shared Amplifier CLI session ID
changes: Chat flyouts show and copy one Session ID matching Amplifier CLI, including chats first created in the CLI. Internal app keys are no longer labeled as session IDs in the flyout.
Find chats by their shared session ID or its prefix. Conversation details use the same ID, and the flyout clarifies that CLI session lists belong to the shown workspace.
Existing session files, saved history, pins and selection are preserved.
This release also includes immediate message delivery feedback and editing within the current conversation, with an explicit option to start a new conversation instead.

notices.title: Message edits stay in the current conversation
notices.detail: Editing a sent message now revises the current conversation by default. Saved revision evidence is retained; external tool effects are not undone or replayed.
notices.action: Select Start a new conversation instead in the edit dialog when you want a separate conversation.

releases.title: Work patch editing and clearer conversation recovery
changes: Work includes contextual patch editing alongside existing file tools. Shared file-access choices apply to both, including older settings and delegated workers.
Agents receive clearer guidance for finding and reading other conversations and using the existing shared app, workspace, voice and permission controls.
Inspect a stopped conversation, copy its session ID or diagnostics, and create a recovery copy that preserves readable history without repeating work. The original conversation is kept.
Updates identify unresolved sources and workspaces. Unregistered bundles in older conversations are shown separately from current configuration problems.
Activity appears beside the action that is running. Dialogs support outside dismissal while preserving in-progress drafts and reporting failures.

releases.title: Stable workspace and chat navigation
changes: Workspace and chat rows keep a fixed height when hovered. Details and actions open in a flyout with full names, copyable paths, session IDs and last activity.
See working, attention and unread indicators directly in the list, and filter working conversations or those needing attention across the complete matching library.
Find workspaces through recent activity or browse nested folders, then open a workspace to give its chats the full sidebar. Duplicate folder names retain distinguishing parent paths.

Keyboard and touch controls, narrow screens and saved themes retain accessible details and actions. Browsing and opening details leave conversation selection, unread state and activity order unchanged.
Failed conversations can also be diagnosed and continued in a safe recovery copy, preserving the original history without replaying work.

notices.title: Navigation details and actions moved
notices.detail: The default sidebar now switches between the workspace index and the selected workspace’s chats. Pin, rename and remove actions are in the details flyout; full filesystem paths remain available there and in search. Saved conversations, registrations and custom shell compositions are preserved.
notices.action: Use Workspaces or All workspaces to browse, and hover a row or choose its … button for details and actions.

releases.title: Conversation export, execution details and feedback follow-up
changes: Copy or download a whole conversation as Markdown, including older saved messages, code, voice transcripts and artifact references. JSON export remains available.

Read complete assistant replies automatically and expand public tool inputs, results and errors. Live timers and usage distinguish pending work from unavailable measurements, including background conversation naming.

Read reports submitted through this host and append follow-up comments to reports owned by its signed-in GitHub account. Drafts and selected reports stay separate between browsers, and retrying a comment does not post it twice.

releases.title: Switch bundles without a required preview
changes: Choose Switch bundle or Fork with this bundle immediately, or use Preview changes first. Both routes are available to app agents too.
Switching reuses the configuration it just validated instead of loading the target bundle again. The menu shows progress immediately and prevents duplicate clicks.
History, compatible model choices, and rollback remain protected. If your pinned model is unavailable, choose whether to use the new bundle’s model before continuing.

releases.title: Continue here from the message box
changes: When another app owns the conversation, a clear overlay covers the message box with a Continue here action. Saved history and navigation remain available.
The message box stays blocked while takeover is pending or has failed. Your draft is preserved, and a failed takeover can be retried explicitly.
The takeover overlay supports keyboard navigation and narrow mobile layouts, and restores typing focus after a successful request when you have stayed in the message box.

releases.title: Work by default and bundle display names
changes: New installations and new conversations without a saved bundle choice use Work. Existing conversations and explicit app, workspace, and shared choices are preserved.
Bundle pickers and repository discovery show the bundle’s own display_name when available, while saved bundle IDs stay unchanged. Choices remain alphabetically sorted.
Display names are read from local or cached manifests and Foundation registry metadata without fetching remote bundles when opening a picker.

notices.title: Work is the default bundle
notices.detail: Work is now the default when no bundle choice is saved. Work currently requires access to its private GitHub repository.
notices.action: Choose a different app or workspace default in Settings if desired; Anchors remains available.

releases.title: Read earlier messages in live conversations
changes: Load earlier messages and automatic scroll-back now work while a conversation runtime is ready or busy.
Earlier pages preserve incoming responses, drafts, and current work, including when new messages have been saved since the last history refresh.
Overlapping page requests keep message identities and reading position; incompatible saved-history changes remain visible as a retryable error.

releases.title: Ready conversations and responsive source checks
changes: Switch between cached conversations immediately while runtime preparation continues in the background, retaining drafts, scroll position, and unsaved artifact edits.
Retain settled conversation workers for reuse, with bounded background preparation and safe retirement that preserves saved history and waits for uncertain replies.
Source checks no longer treat read-only native child sessions or unsupported legacy session IDs as broken resumable configuration.
Large source-usage checks run outside the request thread so the app remains responsive while workspace settings are read.

notices.title: Conversation preparation and retention
notices.detail: Unified now prepares selected conversations in the background and retains up to 32 settled workers for up to 12 hours. This can use additional memory; active work is protected from idle retirement.
notices.action: Review the worker retention controls in Settings if you want different limits or to turn off background preparation.

releases.title: Built-in Work, alphabetical bundles, and accurate source checks
changes: Work is available as a built-in standalone bundle, with existing registrations and source overrides preserved. Bundle choices are sorted alphabetically by their displayed labels.
Standard project and user bundle folders now resolve consistently during conversation preparation and read-only source-usage checks, including directory, Markdown, and YAML bundles.
Historical workspaces with an unresolved directory no longer trigger a misleading source-configuration warning. Their saved history remains available.

releases.title: Interactive surfaces that grow with the conversation
changes: Agents can create interactive interfaces for a conversation and refine them in one tab, with shared controls for users and agents.
Selections and notes survive compatible design updates, restoration and refresh. Unfinished inputs remain protected when changes arrive at the same time.
Review and approve theme previews, application and reversal through host controls. Small palette changes preserve the existing shell skin.
The Unified shell behavior includes repository-owned skills and guides for layouts, extensions and conversation surfaces.

releases.title: Show standalone bundles in conversation pickers
changes: Conversation and default bundle pickers now show built-in conversation profiles and explicit standalone registrations, excluding cached add-ons and source-only aliases.
Capability bundles remain available under Add capabilities. Existing conversations and defaults retain their selections.

releases.title: Choose bundles per conversation and set scoped defaults
changes: Choose a root bundle beside the model, with friendly names and descriptions.
Preview and switch an idle conversation to another bundle, retaining history and compatible model choices; failed loads restore the previous configuration.
Fork with another bundle while preserving the original conversation, saved history, voice references, and artifact snapshots.
Set a default for this Unified app, this workspace on this computer, or shared Amplifier settings, using the same controls available to agents.
Bundle switches replace instructions and reset previous module edits, modes, and budget overrides. Existing conversations keep their roots when a default changes.

releases.title: Flexible artifact viewers with protected unsaved edits
changes: Choose a validated artifact viewer through Open with, including separately built viewers loaded while the app is running.
Pin a second ordinary artifact view while the primary view follows your work; each view keeps its own viewer and settings without changing the saved source or composer target.
Library browsing preserves mounted viewers and unsaved edits. Actions that would discard a declared edit wait for you to finish it or explicitly recover the viewer.
Viewer controls reject stale targets, and missing or failed viewers can fall back to the standard viewer while retaining the saved artifact.

releases.title: Preserve drafts during quick conversation switches
changes: Typing or sending in another conversation no longer cancels an unsaved draft from the previous conversation during its short save delay.
Draft saves stay attached to their original conversation, and sending does not restore stale draft text or send it to a different chat.

releases.title: Reliable restart recovery and saved conversations
changes: Invalid saved restart receipts no longer leave conversations and update actions blocked; the interrupted attempt remains recorded without claiming restart success.
Saved documents, diagrams, images and interactive surfaces reopen with their retained content after a host restart, while preserving conversation selection and unsent drafts.
Voice corrections are delivered to the existing conversation with their original request and approval boundaries intact.
Recovered background-work evidence is clearly labeled as a service update, while messages actually typed by the user retain their original attribution.
An older saved provider selection can resume through a uniquely matching configured instance of the same provider and model, preserving its saved reasoning effort.

releases.title: Reliable provider settings and connection checks
changes: Provider settings, model discovery and connection checks start correctly in the isolated runtime used by installed applications.
A provider helper that exits without a result now reports the exit status and recovery guidance instead of incorrectly saying dependencies are still installing.

releases.title: Preserve canvas resources across clients
changes: Storage cleanup retains canvas content, saved tool views, nested resources and attachments referenced by any client, including disconnected clients.
Startup and routine saves use complete shared and client state when checking which resource files remain in use.
A recovery action can restore missing content from exact hash-matching saved JSON while preserving artifact identities and without replaying tools.
The TUI host recommendation is now 0.11.9 or later; the documented live-client validation baseline remains 0.11.7.

notices.title: Protection for saved Canvas content
notices.detail: Earlier releases could delete resource files still referenced by saved canvas views during cleanup. This release prevents that deletion; it cannot reconstruct content already lost.
notices.action: Install this update. If a saved view reports unavailable content, recover it from an exact retained source or reopen the read-only view. Do not replay a tool action that changes data just to restore its display.
previousTitles: Update to protect saved canvas content

releases.title: Shared model settings for native runtimes
changes: An optional host adapter lets compatible native runtimes read shared provider settings from the user, workspace and native-session scopes while retaining their own domain bundles and instructions.
The adapter uses normal model routing, preserves delegated model preferences and keeps saved-session configuration checks. Installing this release does not enable it or change an existing manager.
A shareable TUI integration guide documents settings precedence, provider instances, credentials, routing, voice preferences and cross-app adoption checks.

releases.title: Reliable live-session activation and terminal client handoff
changes: A new live turn keeps session ownership while it is being scheduled, preventing a concurrent UI control from parking it before execution starts.
The runtime uses the reviewed loop-live scheduling correction across both session preparation and installed runtime dependencies.
The TUI developer handoff documents the supported connection, command, snapshot, retry and lifecycle contracts with validation boundaries.

releases.title: Clearer ecosystem update status
changes: Updates distinguish sources found in shared Amplifier settings from cached sources whose use is unknown, while keeping failures visible and eligible updates available.
Retained conversation history for missing workspace folders no longer causes a source-configuration warning.
Verified wiki-weaver build-generated version stamps no longer block ecosystem updates; genuine edits and unrecognized generated changes remain protected.

releases.title: Updates resume after inspecting runtime settings
changes: Opening a running mount plan or inspecting runtime settings no longer leaves application updates waiting indefinitely when the conversation is idle.
Updates continue to wait for accepted messages, starting workers, active calls, and unfinished runtime controls.
A runtime control that times out or loses its caller remains protected until the worker finishes or exits.

releases.title: Reliable drafts before the first conversation
changes: Typing before the first conversation now saves your draft without a validation error or creating a chat.
The unsent draft survives reload and stays private to that browser. Creating the first conversation carries the draft forward.
Delayed draft saves remain attached to their original composer and cannot overwrite a newly selected conversation.

releases.title: Release history and important update notices
changes: Updates now includes a changelog, with installed release notes available offline and upcoming notes loaded from the exact published release.
High-impact changes show what changed and what to do. Review status is shared across devices; reviewing clears the badge and keeps the notice in the changelog.
Release publishing now requires an authored changelog entry and uses it for GitHub release notes. This history begins with version 0.11.0.

releases.title: Reliable first launch and review acknowledgments
changes: An empty installation now opens with an editable composer; the first message creates one conversation.
Marking an Activity item reviewed stays responsive while a message send is waiting. Reviewing an older item cannot dismiss a newer occurrence.
Release checks now cover empty first launch and reviewing notices during a pending send.

releases.title: Live conversations across windows and devices
changes: Connected web windows and devices share accepted messages, live replies, approvals and running work.
Each browser keeps its own selected conversation, drafts, panels and canvas controls. Reload restores that browser's view; disconnecting leaves work running.
The service API and Python adapter support future terminal clients. A separate TUI application is not included in this release.
Shared configuration introduced in 0.11.0 is preserved.

notices.title: Devices share work and keep separate views
notices.detail: Messages and approvals affect the same live conversation across connected devices. Selecting another conversation or editing an unsent draft now affects only that browser. The first browser to attach inherits saved drafts from the previous shared view.
notices.action: Use the same conversation on another device to follow ongoing work. Check the first attached browser for drafts saved before this upgrade. Closing a browser does not stop the work.

releases.title: Shared Amplifier configuration
changes: Amplifier Unified reads the same ~/.amplifier/settings.yaml as Amplifier CLI, including providers, model routing, bundle defaults and voice preferences.
Workspace .amplifier/settings.yaml and settings.local.yaml override global defaults; existing session overrides remain in effect.
Provider credentials use the shared ~/.amplifier/keys.env and routing profiles use shared Amplifier locations.

notices.title: Settings now apply across Amplifier apps
notices.detail: Shared ~/.amplifier configuration is now authoritative. Changes to shared providers, routing and voice preferences can affect CLI and Unified sessions. Migration preserves existing shared values and keeps a backup of the previous private Unified settings; conflicting private values are not copied over shared values.
notices.action: Review providers, model routing and voice preferences after upgrading. Put project-specific choices in the workspace's .amplifier settings. If an old Unified choice is missing, compare the migration backup under ~/.amplifier-unified/backups/shared-settings-* before changing shared values.
